title: Detection Rule
description: Contract for a single analytics/detection rule in this repo. Every YAML file under detections/ must validate against this schema. additionalProperties is false at every object level: an unrecognised key is a hard failure, never a silently ignored one.

id.description: Stable UUIDv4 identity for the rule. Never change this once the rule ships; it is the join key to fixtures, incidents and tuning history.

title.description: Human-readable rule name as it appears in the SIEM.

status.description: Lifecycle stage. Only 'production' rules should page a human.

created.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be quoted in YAML or PyYAML converts it to a date object.

modified.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be quoted in YAML.

description.description: What the rule detects, in plain language, for the analyst reading the incident at 3am.

rationale.description: Why this is worth detecting: the attacker capability it removes or exposes.

tables.description: Log Analytics table names the query reads. Drives fixture generation in tests/.

connector.description: Sentinel data connector that populates the tables.

dcr_required.description: True when a Data Collection Rule must be deployed for these tables to populate.

ingestion_cost.description: free = no ingestion charge (e.g. AzureActivity). billed-high = think before enabling.

technique.description: T#### or T####.### for a sub-technique.

confidence.description: How much you trust a hit to be real, independent of how bad it would be.

query_frequency.description: How often the rule runs. ISO 8601 duration, e.g. PT1H, PT5M, P1D.

query_period.description: How far back each run looks. ISO 8601 duration. Should be >= query_frequency or you create blind spots between runs.

trigger_threshold.description: Alert when result count <operator> threshold. gt/0 is the common 'any hit alerts' case.

entity_mappings.description: Maps query output columns onto SIEM entities so incidents correlate. Identifiers are a list of {name, column} pairs rather than a free-form map, so additionalProperties:false can still catch typos.

name.description: SIEM identifier name, e.g. FullName, Address, ResourceId.

column.description: Column produced by the rule query. Leading underscore is legal (_ResourceId).

lookback.description: ISO 8601 duration. Alerts within this window collapse into one incident.

group_by.description: Entity types to group on. Must be entity types this rule actually maps.

false_positives.description: Known benign causes. Non-empty by design: if you cannot name one, you have not thought about the rule hard enough to ship it.

validation.description: How this rule was proven to work. Mirrors the repo's negative-then-positive test philosophy.

reference.description: Pointer to the proof: an Atomic test ID, a runbook, or a doc path.

fixture.description: Path to the test fixture, relative to the project root. Null when method is 'none'.

runbook.description: Path to the analyst runbook, relative to the project root.

playbook.description: Automated Logic App / playbook name, or null if none.

auto_response_tier.description: none = human only. enrich = gather context. notify = page. contain = takes action on production.

tuning_history.description: Append-only log of why the rule changed. Empty array is valid for a brand new rule.

query.description: The KQL detection logic, verbatim. Phase 3 prepends datatable() fixtures to this string unmodified.
